That’s a real code, not just a habit — “thank you and move on” is how you were raised to handle praise without making yourself the center of it.

But there’s a difference between *moving on* and *handing it back*. “Thanks, glad it helped” and then changing the subject is moving on. “Thanks — she did all the real work” is moving on by giving the thing away. One accepts it and closes it; the other makes sure it doesn’t stay with you.

You don’t have to stand there and take it. You just don’t have to pass it to someone else on your way out.

What would “thanks, glad it helped” and then straight to the next thing feel like — still uncomfortable, or just unfamiliar?
